title: DIC Payment Calendar and Returned-Payment Thresholds
content:
Payment operations figures for Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) paid to surviving spouses. The four figures below apply without variation to all six rate categories (DIC Surviving Spouse (Basic Rate), DIC Surviving Spouse (Basic Rate with 8-Year Provision), DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound), DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound with 8-Year Provision), DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance) and DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance with 8-Year Provision)).

| Figure | Value | Unit and meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Payment day | 1 | Day of the following month on which a monthly payment is issued (the 1st) |
| Account-change lead time | 10 | Minimum calendar days before a payment date that an account change must be recorded to apply to that payment |
| Returned-payment suspension count | 2 | Number of returned payments within the window that require suspension of the award |
| Returned-payment window | 12 | Length, in months, of the rolling window over which returned payments are counted |

## The returned-payment window

The window is a rolling period of 12 calendar months ending on the current date. Returned payments on the award are counted in it by the date the funds came back, not by the entitlement month of the payment that was returned.

## Illustrations (hypothetical dates)

**Payment day.** Under a payment day of 1, the monthly payment for the month of March is issued on April 1, the 1st of the following month.

**Account-change lead time.** For a payment issued on the 1st of a month, a change recorded 10 calendar days before that date meets the 10-day lead time; a change recorded 9 calendar days before it does not.

**Counting returned payments.** On the current date, a returned payment whose funds came back 11 months earlier is inside the 12-month window; one whose funds came back 13 months earlier is outside it. Two returned payments inside the window reach the suspension count of 2; one does not.
